claims.text: Conventional deposition routes typically produce high-entropy-alloy bond coats with heterogeneous microstructures, higher porosity, and higher defect density.
HVOF deposition with controlled post-deposition cooling produces rapid solidification.
Optimized HVOF processing will refine and homogenize the bond-coat microstructure.
Optimized HVOF processing will reduce bond-coat porosity and interfacial defect density.
A refined, homogeneous microstructure with fewer defects promotes stronger oxide-scale adhesion.
Reduced porosity and fewer interfacial defects delay crack initiation.
Rapid solidification during HVOF processing minimizes grain coarsening and defect formation.
Minimizing grain coarsening and defects reduces sites for oxidation and crack nucleation under cyclic stress.
The HVOF-induced microstructure improves resistance to thermal fatigue and oxidation.
HVOF-processed bond coats will have a longer thermal-cycling lifetime than conventionally processed bond coats.
HVOF-processed bond coats will show enhanced oxidation resistance relative to conventionally processed bond coats.
The resulting increases in cyclic lifetime and oxidation resistance will improve reliability in high-temperature applications.
The improvement is expected to persist during repeated thermal cycling above 1000°C within the tested thermal-barrier-coating operating range.
The improvement may not persist under extreme thermal gradients or prolonged chemical attack beyond the evaluated conditions.
